## Definitions

### `production.wo_lead_time` — Work-order lead time

- **Module / unit / direction:** production · hours · lower_better
- **Gate:** `production.dashboard.view` (permission-derived; no role-name branch)
- **Answered by:** `App\Modules\Dashboard\Services\Analytics\Domains\WorkOrderLeadTimeAnalytics`
- **Aggregation:** AVG(actual_end - actual_start) in hours per calendar month via date_trunc, over work orders that have both timestamps inside the window; COUNT(*) of those orders alongside.
- **Sources:** `work_orders.actual_start`, `work_orders.actual_end`, `work_orders.machine_id`
- **Indexes relied on:** `work_orders_actual_start_index`, `work_orders_actual_end_index`, `work_orders_machine_id_index`
- **Refresh / cache:** live · TTL from `dashboard.analytics.cache_ttl_seconds`
- **Known caveats:**
  - Only completed work orders (both timestamps set) are counted — open WOs are excluded, not zeroed.
  - No target lead time exists in settings, so the tile shows the average with no target band.
  - Elapsed wall-clock hours include nights and weekends; it is not machine-hours.

### `returns.pipeline` — Returns pipeline

- **Module / unit / direction:** returns · count · lower_better
- **Gate:** `return_management.view` (permission-derived; no role-name branch)
- **Answered by:** `App\Modules\Dashboard\Services\Analytics\Domains\ReturnsPipelineAnalytics`
- **Aggregation:** COUNT(*) grouped by `return_requests.status` and by `type` over the selected window, plus a FILTER count for `pending_approval` and MIN(return_date) for the oldest open return. All counts computed by the database.
- **Sources:** `return_requests.status`, `return_requests.type`, `return_requests.return_date`
- **Indexes relied on:** `return_requests_status_index`, `return_requests_type_index`, `return_requests_return_date_index`
- **Refresh / cache:** live · TTL from `dashboard.analytics.cache_ttl_seconds`
- **Known caveats:**
  - Counts returns, not return lines — line-level quantities live on return_request_items.
  - Returns whose `return_date` is null are outside every window (they exist but have no date to filter on).
  - Statuses are the current state; there is no status history, so a dwell-time reading needs audit_logs.

## Conventions

- Aggregation happens in SQL (`date_trunc`, `COUNT(*) FILTER`, `AVG`) — never by loading rows
  into PHP and looping.
- Every payload is cached per `scope + filters` with the metric TTL; `flush($code)` bumps a
  version counter (works on array and Redis stores alike), which is the explicit-invalidation seam.
- Row scope is the owning module's policy/scope code, never re-expressed here.
- Snapshot-grained metrics (the `kpi.*` family) stay monthly and are read from `kpi_snapshots`;
  anything sub-month aggregates the source tables.
